subject: Inference mode fit & sunset plan
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@medscribe.ai>, Carlos Ramirez <carlos@veridian.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-24T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Quick recap + next steps (deployment mode & migration questions)

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great conversation. Quick written recap and a small set of asks so we can size options and propose a clear POC.

High-level notes from our call:
- Primary product surface: clinical summarization and patient Q&A (PHI in some flows).
- Current stack: Anthropic API for prototyping; a small on-prem GPU cluster (NVIDIA A40/80 equivalent) for sensitive workflows.
- Non-functional priorities: sub-250ms p95 for public traffic, SOC 2 compliance + HITRUST roadmap, and hard data residency requirements for EU/US West.

Two decision axes we discussed: Hosted API vs Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private (VPC / on-prem). You mentioned a preference for Dedicated for volume-facing endpoints and Private for PHI workflows, but we need a couple of confirmations to recommend architecture and POC scope. Could you confirm the following?
1) Expected steady-state qps and peak concurrency (per model/endpoint).
2) Which workflows will include PHI (and whether PHI must remain on your network at all times).
3) Any procurement or legal constraints that would push for Private first (e.g., must have on-prem in contract).
4) Current SLAs with Anthropic and any migration blackout windows.

Proposed next steps if you're aligned:
- You send the short infra + traffic doc (one-pager) — we can use the diagram you referenced as a starting point.
- Redwood provides a POC plan that shows: Dedicated for public traffic + Private VPC route for PHI during canary, with clear rollback. (Estimate: 2-week POC + 2-week canary).
- Tech sync with Karthik and David to validate bandwidth/egress, KV cache behavior, and model variant parity.

I'll attach a simple POC outline in the follow-up. Thanks — appreciate the clarity.

--
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-11-25T09:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps (deployment mode & migration questions)

Thanks Grace — helpful recap. Answers inline: 

1) Traffic: baseline ~4–6 qps (sustained), expected peak ~25 qps during spikes (monthly batch jobs + live peak). Concurrent requests per second typically 8–12 during spikes.
2) PHI: the clinical summarization pipeline handles PHI and must remain within our private network for production; lower-risk Q&A can be routed through a hosted endpoint. We can accept Dedicated for non-PHI.
3) Procurement: legal requires HITRUST or equivalent controls in contract for PHI workflows. Procurement timeline is ~6–8 weeks; we have an internal security review scheduled Dec 10.
4) Anthropic SLA: currently best-effort with 99.5% availability; no blackout windows planned but we'd like a staged cutover.

Attaching current_infra_diagram.png which shows on-prem cluster & latency path. A couple of follow-ups from our side: how would you handle token auditing for PHI flows, and do you support split routing (part Dedicated, part Private) without degrading P95 latency?

Samantha
VP Product, MediScribe
samantha@medscribe.ai
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha@medscribe.ai>, Carlos Ramirez <carlos@veridian.com>
Date: 2026-11-26T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Quick recap + next steps (deployment mode & migration questions)

Looping you both in — Samantha confirmed traffic and PHI constraints (see below). Key asks:
- Karthik: can you summarize latency/quantization tradeoffs if we recommend Dedicated for non-PHI and Private for PHI? Specifically: p95 impact for int8/4-bit quantized LLMs at 512-token avg context and 1024 token worst-case. Also note KV cache behavior between Dedicated and Private (is cache shared or per deployment?).
- David: migration risks from their legacy on-prem GPU cluster — what does a dual-write + traffic split cutover look like? Any gotchas around model parity when migrating from Anthropic API to an open model we host or to our managed variants?

Suggested POC approach to propose back to Samantha:
1) Week 0: connectivity & compliance checklist exchange (secure tunnel, firewall rules, audit requirements).
2) Week 1–2: POC — host a recommended model on Dedicated, run non-PHI traffic and measure p95.
3) Week 3–4: Private VPC pilot for PHI flows with strict egress controls; run a small portion of traffic via canary.
4) Post-POC: cutover plan + a 2-week canary with rollback.

I'll draft the POC plan and share the PDF. Thoughts?

--
Grace
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@medscribe.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-30T11:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Inference mode fit & sunset plan — initial technical guidance and POC attachments

Thanks for the context, Samantha — and Grace, thanks for the recap. Short technical answers we can include in the POC PDF (attached). Highlights: 

- Latency/quantization: For 512-token average context, int8 quantization on an A100-class node typically adds ~10–20ms per token compared to fp16 but reduces memory enough to increase batch sizes; p95 impact is workload dependent but we've measured sub-200ms p95 for typical summarization models at 10 qps on Dedicated with batching tuned. For 1024 tokens, tail latency increases — plan to reserve headroom or use shorter context windows for public endpoints.
- KV cache & routing: Cache is per-deployment by default. We can provide cache-warming and prefix caching to keep PHI flows performant in Private. Shared cache across Dedicated and Private deployments is possible via a managed cache service but adds operational complexity and potential egress constraints.
- Split routing: Supported. Our smart routing layer can send traffic by policy (path, model variant, region). The important tradeoff is cold-starts for Private variants; we recommend a steady keepalive and warmup traffic during canary.
- Legacy GPU migration: dual-write approach works — mirror requests to Redwood and legacy cluster, compare outputs, and slowly shift percentages. Biggest gotcha: tokenizer/model differences produce semantic diffs; include an eval set to validate parity and an output-tolerance threshold.

Attached: redwood_poc_plan.pdf (detailed timeline), connectivity_playbook.md (tunnel & firewall checklist).

Next step: Grace, can you propose dates for the Week 0 kickoff? Samantha — if Dec 14 week works, we can reserve Dedicated capacity for the POC and schedule a security sync on Dec 10.

--
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Technical Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
